title: Nioh Was Announced 13 Years Before It Came Out
hook:
Nioh was announced in 2004 with an Akira Kurosawa script and didn't ship until 2017, after being remade three times. This week it got its first ever Xbox date. Would you wait 13 years for a game?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Nioh was announced in two thousand four, about thirteen years before anyone could play it? Back then Koei revealed a PlayStation Three game called Oni. It was built around an unfinished script by the famous film director Akira Kurosawa. Koei planned it as a traditional Japanese role playing game. The project stalled, and over the years it was remade from scratch three times. First it was a turn based RPG inside Koei. Then the studio Omega Force turned it into an action RPG. Finally Team Ninja, the studio behind Ninja Gaiden, rebuilt it as the brutal samurai action game we know today. Koei Tecmo founder Yoichi Erikawa later admitted the long wait was his own fault. He said if anyone working under him had spent twelve years on one game, they would have been fired. The game finally shipped on PlayStation Four in twenty seventeen and became a hit. This week Koei Tecmo announced the series is coming to Xbox for the first time ever. Nioh Three and its Complete Edition land on Xbox Series on January twenty eighth, twenty twenty seven, right before the franchise turns ten years old. Would you wait thirteen years for a game? Follow for more gaming history.
